stability: Every entry in `outputs` is stable API: the keys, the invariant scoring/status fields, and the field names/nesting shown in each example. Removing or renaming any of them is a breaking change and requires a TOOL_VERSION bump plus a changelog note here. This target writes NO consumer-facing output files — both entries are kind `inline`: search results ride the search_content response and index jobs report counts via get_job_status. Per-document PAYLOAD fields vary by collection schema (each schema's `result_fields`); the scoring fields are invariant. Anything on S3 (`_lancedb_index/` storage layout, `_search/` transients such as vectors.json, row-group objects) is internal and may change or vanish without notice.

search-results.description: Ranked per-document hits returned inline by search_content — use for: rendering ranked hits, deep-linking into assets by timestamp (asset_id + start_ms/end_ms)

results.text: A reporter interviews the senator about the bill.
results.title: Evening News

example.search_term: Jane Doe on a stormy beach

search-results.notes: INVARIANT per doc: doc_id, asset_id, start_ms, end_ms, score (raw ANN cosine or FTS relevance), rrf_score (within-index score-weighted RRF aggregate), match_sources ({sub_query: contribution} — which ANN/FTS sub-queries surfaced the doc), source_index (the scope that surfaced it: shot/scene/segment/utterance/topic), final_score (cross-index score normalized to [0,1], top hit = 1.0 — the sort key). SCHEMA-DEPENDENT payload: the collection schema's result_fields per doc_type (default schemas: scene → text/named_entities/segment_parent_id, shot → frame_s3_key/scene_parent_id, segment → text, utterance → text/scene_parent_id/topic_parent_id, topic → text/named_entities). CONDITIONAL: highlights ({field: text with matched tokens wrapped in <em>}) on FTS matches only; title/genres only when asset_metadata was registered at indexing. skipped_indices lists scopes that were NOT searched: index not yet registered, no docs, or dropped at decompose (no runnable sub-queries) — it is how a caller tells 'no matches' from 'never searched' — a graceful miss, not an error.

index-status.description: get_job_status SUCCEEDED counts for an index_content job — use for: verifying an indexing run landed (prepared/skipped/indexed)
index-status.notes: prepared = documents embedded into rows this run; skipped = per-document dedup hits (doc_id = md5(collection:asset:doc_type:start_ms:end_ms:chunk_idx) already indexed — a full resubmit legitimately reports prepared=0, skipped=N, indexed=0); indexed = rows written, summed across the per-table Map iterations — prepared == indexed on success. FAILED/TIMED_OUT/ABORTED responses replace the counts with `error`.
